title: The Kitten and the Broken Jug

pages.text: This is {name}. {name} is a little striped kitten with white paws and a tail that hooks at the tip. Morning fills the cosy cottage with the smell of warm milk, while the grandmother cat hums a soft tune. Soft little ears catch grandmother's song, and a small heart purrs along. {name} sniffs at the warm milky smell, and tiny whiskers tremble with joy.

{name} rolls that soft little ball across the floor — this way and that, this way and that. The ball bounces over the striped rug, and quick white paws chase happily after it. It swishes along the rug — and that is the merriest sound in the whole cottage. "One more time!" {name} purrs merrily. The little hooked tail dances too — up and down, up and down. The morning is so bright it makes {name} want to play and play.

The ball rolls faster, and {name} dashes after it faster still, giggling inside. Paws patter, ears twitch, and that hooked tail bounces along. The little breeze of running tickles tiny whiskers. "Oh, what fun!" {name} mews brightly. A small heart leaps along with the ball — light and happy. The game grows louder and bolder — hop, skip, one more time!

The ball bounces high — and flies straight toward the table. On the table stands grandmother's favourite jug, all painted with little flowers. {name} freezes for one short breath. "Uh-oh!" {name} breathes out softly. The little paws want to catch the ball, but it flies faster than the wind.

Clink! The jug wobbles, tips, and breaks into little pieces. {name} stands very still, and a small heart taps quick and soft: tap-tap-tap. That little "clink" still rings inside tiny ears. Even the hooked tail lies quiet and does not stir. The whole cottage goes very, very quiet.

{name} glances at the door — did grandmother hear? The room is empty, only the little shards lying on the floor. "What do I do now?" thinks {name}. The shards lie so quietly, as if they are waiting for an answer too. Inside, something feels ticklish and a little bit shy.

Quick-quick, {name} gathers the shards with soft paws and tucks them behind the curtain. The paws work fast-fast, while little ears listen for every rustle. The curtain sways and hides the secret away. "No one will see," whispers {name}, but the little voice sounds ever so small. There now — as if nothing ever happened.

Grandmother comes in and smiles gently: "Time for some milk." {name} sits by the little bowl, but somehow the milk does not taste the same. {name} takes another small sip and sighs quietly. Grandmother's smile is so warm that it makes a little nose tingle. The secret already sits inside, small and heavy.

{name} picks up the ball again, but the game just will not play. "Let's play," {name} whispers softly to the ball. But it only lies there quietly, not nearly as bouncy as in the morning. Paws do not want to run, and ears keep listening toward the curtain. Somewhere behind it hides that clink-and-shard.

{name} lies down quietly on the rug and lets out a little sigh. The rug is warm and kind, but somehow play does not call anymore. The thoughts keep rolling back to the curtain, like a little ball that only rolls one way. The sun leans lower, and the cottage fills with a warm amber glow. And the secret grows heavier and heavier, like a small pebble in the chest.

The curtain sways softly in a little draft — hush, hush. {name} listens — and it seems to whisper about the hidden thing. "Hush, hush," the curtain says again, and the secret behind it seems to stir. {name} mews very softly: if only that whisper would go quiet. Ears press down, and that hooked tail tucks in close and small.

{name} tries to play a little more, to sip a little more milk — but nothing feels right. The smile has hidden itself away together with the shards. Even the warm rug does not feel as soft as it always does. "Maybe I should tell grandmother?" {name} wonders for the very first time, and a small heart quietly answers: yes. Oh, how heavy it is, this little secret.

Outside the evening turns blue, and grandmother lights the warm lamp. The cottage glows soft and cosy, while {name} keeps thinking and thinking. The lamp hums with warm light, as if it is gently cheering too. The words are very close now — right at the tip of a little tongue. Perhaps it is time to be brave?

{name} takes one small step toward grandmother. Then another — and another. The floor creaks softly under small paws: creak-creak. "I can do it," {name} breathes. The white paws tremble just a little, but a small heart whispers: the truth is lighter than the secret.

"Grandmother," {name} mews softly, "it was me — the jug fell and broke because of me. The pieces are behind the curtain. I'm sorry." The words fly out at last. Grandmother listens very quietly and is not cross, not even a tiny bit. And right away — oh! — inside it feels lighter and lighter. The little heart beats steadier, and the cottage feels warm and safe again.

Grandmother leans down, and {name} melts into her warm hug. Her soft fur smells of milk and home. "Thank you for telling the truth," she purrs gently. "The truth can be scary for a moment, but it stays light forever." {name} purrs back, and the two purrs blend into one gentle little song. A small heart glows warm and light, right down to the tip of the hooked tail. Little ears settle close, and everything feels cosy and safe again.

Together they lift the shards out from behind the curtain and lay them on the table. {name} hands grandmother one piece after another. The little shards tinkle softly, as if saying hello. "We will mend it all," says grandmother gently. Now there is no secret left — only the warm lamplight.

Grandmother mends the shards with glue that leaves a golden line. {name} holds each little piece steady with soft paws. "Right there, just so," grandmother purrs gently. Small paws and grandmother's big paws work together — unhurried, careful, and kind. Slowly the jug becomes whole again — only now with veins of gold.

There — all done! The jug stands on the table once more, a bright golden line winding down its side. It glimmers in the lamplight like a tiny warm river. Grandmother's words still glow in a small heart: our jug has a special little story of its own now. {name} looks and purrs softly: now it is the loveliest jug in the whole house.

That evening {name} curls into a cosy ball on grandmother's lap, the golden jug glowing softly nearby. Inside it now lives the most honest little story in the whole house. Grandmother's purring rocks like a soft, soft lullaby. Little eyes slowly drift closed, and everything inside feels light as a feather. Goodnight, warm and truthful little heart!
